name: GitHub CLI auth (token from a runtime env var)
description: Authenticates the GitHub CLI (`gh`) from a token supplied at runtime — picked up automatically via an --env-file in runArgs, no shell-sourcing required — so issues and pull requests can be read and filed from inside the container. Installation of `gh` itself is left to the official github-cli feature, which this declares a dependency on; what is added here is the auth wiring. `gh` reads GH_TOKEN from the environment natively, so nothing is written to disk for the CLI itself; the attach script instead runs `gh auth setup-git`, which teaches git to push and clone over HTTPS with the same token. That part must be reasserted on every attach, since VS Code re-copies ~/.gitconfig from the host on each connect and would otherwise drop the credential helper. A missing token is a skip, not a failure.

tokenEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding the GitHub token. `gh` reads GH_TOKEN (then GITHUB_TOKEN) natively, so leaving this at the default means the CLI is authenticated with no further work. Setting it to any other name makes the attach script re-export that value as GH_TOKEN for interactive shells.

host.description: GitHub host the token authenticates against, as a bare hostname. Set to a GitHub Enterprise hostname to target that instance; the token is then also exported as GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, which is what gh requires for non-github.com hosts.

setupGit.description: Run `gh auth setup-git` on attach, so `git push`/`git clone` over HTTPS authenticate with the same token. Reasserted every attach because VS Code re-copies ~/.gitconfig from the host on each connect. Turn off if you push over SSH and want git left alone.
